Verdict

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators — overall risk: info.

Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators.

The main pre-scan alerts were not validated as malicious evidence:

  • The raw.githubusercontent.com reference appears only in README/PKG-INFO as a Ruff badge URL, not as executable code or an upload path.
  • OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, and similar names are used by the CLI for user-selected LLM providers; there is no evidence of broad environment dumping or secret discovery.
  • The many re.compile(...) matches appear to be document template, placeholder, and pattern-recognition regexes, not obfuscated loader logic.
  • zipfile usage is consistent with .docx processing, since DOCX is ZIP-based; it is not evidence of harvested-file archiving or staging.

Automatic Execution Paths

  • In the provided corpus, there is no evidence of .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, malicious install-time setup.py, abused PEP 517 build hooks, or malicious import-time side effects.
  • The template-engine CLI described in README and implemented in src/engine/cli.py appears to require explicit user invocation, so it is not an install-time or interpreter-start automatic execution path.
  • The provider dynamic imports in src/engine/cli.py occur when a user selects a provider through the CLI and look like normal plugin-style behavior, not an automatic loader/dropper path.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Stealth

  • **Credential harvesting:** No evidence of broad os.environ dumping, .env scanning, SSH key discovery, cloud credential theft, GitHub/PyPI/npm token search, CI secret harvesting, kubeconfig access, or wallet discovery. Reading a single documented provider API-key environment variable appears benign.
  • **Exfiltration / staging:** No evidence of attacker-controlled domains, webhooks, raw IPs, paste/drop services, HTTP exfiltration, or archive staging of harvested files. openrouter.ai/api/v1 appears to be a normal LLM provider API endpoint.
  • **Persistence:** No evidence of cron, systemd units, launch agents, shell profile modification, startup folders, background polling loops, or self-reinstall behavior.
  • **Lateral movement:** No evidence of Kubernetes service-account use, Docker socket access, cloud metadata access, CI publish token theft, GitHub Actions workflow injection, or package registry token reuse.
  • **Obfuscation / loader:** The provided code shows no evidence of eval, exec, compile, marshal, pickle, base64/zlib/gzip payload loading, XOR, downloader stubs, platform-specific RAT selection, or self-deleting droppers.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • Based on the provided file contents, there is no evidence of hidden payloads, unexplained native binaries, abnormal .dist-info contents, sudden malicious dependency insertion, or typosquatting.
  • The dependencies appear aligned with document processing, LLM providers, CLI behavior, and testing; no evidence ties them to supply-chain malware behavior.
  • This review is based mainly on selected sdist text, so wheel/sdist mismatch could not be assessed.

Additional Verification Needed

  • Only selected text from 86 extracted files was provided; pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, entry_points.txt, and parts of the full source/test tree were not included in the corpus. The full files should be checked to confirm build hooks and entry point details.
  • No wheel artifact was provided, so payload differences between sdist and wheel were not verified.
  • The provided text corpus cannot fully rule out hidden binary or large-file payloads outside the selected content.
